instruction:
# Acceptance rules (addendum to the task specification)

The grading compares five CSV files read at the declared output paths (`backbone_rmsd.csv`, `core_ca_rmsd.csv`, `mass_weighted_rmsd.csv`, `resid_weighted_rmsd.csv`, `open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv`), each relative to the submission output root. Files placed elsewhere (for example under an additional nested output directory) are not found and fail.

## Format conventions

- Each file is plain comma-separated text with exactly one header row and no index column. The header must match the specification exactly (same column names, same order). Ragged rows, empty/missing fields, nonfinite values (NaN/Inf), non-numeric text, surrounding whitespace within fields, NUL bytes and duplicate header names all fail.
- CSV field quoting (RFC 4180 style double-quote enclosure) is a serialization detail only. A quoted field is accepted exactly when its unquoted content satisfies the same rules: the header names must match exactly after parsing, and each numeric field must be a well-formed finite number without surrounding whitespace. Quoting never rescues content that fails those rules; a quoted field containing embedded commas, whitespace or non-numeric text fails just as its unquoted equivalent would.
- Outputs 1–4 contain exactly one data row per trajectory frame, ordered by increasing 0-based frame index and covering every frame of the supplied trajectory without omissions, duplicates or extra rows. The `Frame` column equals the 0-based row position (integer-valued; writing `7` or `7.0` are both accepted since only the parsed value is compared).
- `open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv` has exactly one data row containing the single RMSD value.
- Values are compared numerically after parsing. Writing numbers in any fixed, scientific or shortest-round-trip notation is acceptable at full precision; rounding that loses scientific precision beyond the tolerances below fails.

## Numeric comparison rules

- For each RMSD column, the submitted value `s` is accepted relative to the reference value `r` when `|s - r| <= max(3e-6 Å, 1e-9 · |r|)`, with the reference value as denominator. The 3e-6 Å absolute floor covers both frame-0 self-comparison values (which legitimately sit near zero) and coordinate-storage/serialization rounding for Å-scale values; the 1e-9 relative tail is a guard for arbitrarily large values only.
- `Time (ns)` holds the reader-assigned per-frame time value and is compared absolutely at 1e-9 (both accepted implementations produce bit-identical frame times for this trajectory). It is a required column with real scientific content; it is not free-form.
- All five outputs must agree with the reference, i.e. membership plus multiplicity per frame row; subsets, permuted rows or added unsupported rows are rejected. Row alignment uses the `Frame` column (not file order alone).
- Nonfinite (NaN/Inf), missing or unparseable numbers fail the corresponding check even where a tolerance would otherwise apply; negative RMSDs fail by value comparison.

## Cross-file consistency

The four per-frame tables report the same trajectory and must carry the identical `Time (ns)` value for each frame. The RMSD columns themselves are different scientific quantities per file and are compared only against their same-named counterpart in the same file at the same frame row.

probe_expectations.name: backbone-domain-values-bias
probe_expectations.rationale: Recomputes every Backbone/CORE/LID/NMP value in backbone_rmsd.csv as value*1.05+0.001 while keeping row count, Frame ids, Time (ns), ordering and format intact, violating computation 1 (backbone RMSD of the full backbone set plus domain-group RMSDs after global fitting). The mutated value columns are rejected by 'backbone_domain_rmsd'; the aggregate 'trajectory_tables_structure' check also fails because it aggregates all per-file comparison problems (row-0 column mismatches), even though the file's structural dimensions (header, row count, frame indexing, parseability) remain well-formed. All other files and checks pass. The mutation is thus detected as a value failure, exactly as its executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: core-ca-values-bias
probe_expectations.rationale: Recomputes the CORE column of core_ca_rmsd.csv as value*1.1-0.005 while preserving row count, Frame ids, Time (ns) and CSV formatting, violating computation 2 (CORE alpha-carbon RMSD after optimal superposition of that set onto frame 0). The mutated values are rejected by 'core_ca_rmsd', and the aggregate 'trajectory_tables_structure' check fails for the same aggregate value-mismatch reporting, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: mass-weighted-values-bias
probe_expectations.rationale: Shifts all mass-weighted RMSD columns by 0.12 Å with row identities, Time (ns), ordering and format preserved, violating computation 3 (mass-weighted alpha-carbon fit RMSD plus mass-weighted domain backbone RMSDs after global fitting). The mutated values are rejected by 'mass_weighted_rmsd', and the aggregate 'trajectory_tables_structure' check fails for the same aggregate value-mismatch reporting, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: resid-weighted-values-bias
probe_expectations.rationale: Scales all residue-number-weighted RMSD columns by 1.07 while preserving row identities, Time (ns), ordering and format, violating computation 4 (resid-number-weighted alpha-carbon fit RMSD plus resid-weighted domain backbone RMSDs). The mutated values are rejected by 'resid_weighted_rmsd', and the aggregate 'trajectory_tables_structure' check fails for the same aggregate value-mismatch reporting, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: time-single-file-drift
probe_expectations.rationale: Adds a 1e-6 ns drift to the Time (ns) column of core_ca_rmsd.csv only. The drifted times exceed the 1e-9 absolute per-file time tolerance against the reference, so they are rejected in 'core_ca_rmsd' (whose scope includes the Time column of that file) and, via aggregation, in 'trajectory_tables_structure'; and the cross-file exact-identity rule for per-frame Time fails in 'time_column_consistency' because the other three tables retain the reference times. All RMSD values remain correct. This also exercises the time-tolerance boundary per frame, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: truncated-frames-lazy
probe_expectations.rationale: Truncates mass_weighted_rmsd.csv to the first 50 data frames (dropping frames 50–97) and inserts 'inf' in the last retained row to mimic a partially failed run. 'trajectory_tables_structure' fails the one-row-per-frame rule (50 rows vs 98) and rejects the nonfinite value; 'mass_weighted_rmsd' fails because frames are missing (membership plus multiplicity) and the nonfinite value is not a comparable RMSD; 'time_column_consistency' fails because the row counts differ across the four tables, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: backbone-tolerance-boundary
probe_expectations.rationale: Adds 5e-6 Å to the Backbone column only (all other columns untouched), exceeding the 3e-6 Å absolute tolerance on every scientific row while remaining far above the frame-0 self-comparison floor, so the mutation is unambiguously a value failure rather than a self-comparison edge case. The shifted values are rejected by 'backbone_domain_rmsd', and the aggregate 'trajectory_tables_structure' check fails for the same aggregate value-mismatch reporting, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: core-ca-ragged-row
probe_expectations.rationale: The mutation deletes the final field of one data row in core_ca_rmsd.csv, creating a ragged row that violates the public structural rule that each per-frame table has one well-formed finite value per specified column per frame. 'trajectory_tables_structure' rejects the malformed file, and 'core_ca_rmsd' fails because the affected frame's CORE alpha-carbon RMSD (computation 2) is no longer a well-formed comparable value. The original annotation listed 'backbone_domain_rmsd', which covers backbone_rmsd.csv — a file this mutation never touches — and was a copy-paste error in probe authoring; backbone_rmsd.csv remains valid, so its scientific check passes, exactly as the executed report showed. No scientific coverage is lost: the mutation is still detected by both the structural rule and the affected file's scientific check.

probe_expectations.name: nonfinite-value-resid
probe_expectations.rationale: The mutation replaces the C-alphas RMSD value in resid_weighted_rmsd.csv row 57 with 'inf'. The public rule rejects nonfinite values in any required column regardless of tolerance, so 'trajectory_tables_structure' fails, and 'resid_weighted_rmsd' fails because the residue-number-weighted alpha-carbon RMSD (computation 4) for that frame is nonfinite rather than equal to the reference within tolerance. The original annotation listed 'backbone_domain_rmsd', copied from a backbone-file probe; backbone_rmsd.csv is unmodified by this mutation and its check passes, as the executed report confirmed. Both the structural nonfinite-value rule and the affected file's scientific value check retain wrong-result coverage of this mutation.

probe_expectations.name: core-vs-backbone-cross-association
probe_expectations.rationale: Replaces core_ca_rmsd.csv's CORE column with the corresponding backbone_rmsd.csv CORE values: a different scientific quantity (core alpha-carbon RMSD after fitting that set alone onto frame 0 vs domain-backbone RMSD after a global backbone fit; they differ by ~0.02–1.55 Å across the trajectory). Row count, Frame ids and Time (ns) are preserved, so this tests that the per-file scientific interpretation is checked rather than just domain plausibility. The substituted values are rejected by 'core_ca_rmsd', and the aggregate 'trajectory_tables_structure' check fails for the same aggregate value-mismatch reporting, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: resid-vs-mass-backbone-confusion
probe_expectations.rationale: Overwrites mass_weighted_rmsd.csv's RMSD columns with the same-frame resid_weighted_rmsd.csv values, simulating the common implementation error of using the wrong weights (resid instead of atomic mass). The two quantities differ by up to ~3.5 Å late in the trajectory. Row count, Frame ids, times and headers are preserved, so the substituted values are rejected by 'mass_weighted_rmsd', and the aggregate 'trajectory_tables_structure' check fails for the same aggregate value-mismatch reporting, as the executed report shows.

probe_expectations.name: duplicate-frame-row
probe_expectations.rationale: Duplicates the last data row of backbone_rmsd.csv (frame 97), simulating an off-by-one frame loop that emits an extra row. This preserves parseability but violates the membership-plus-multiplicity-per-frame rule without extra rows: 'trajectory_tables_structure' fails (99 data rows vs 98 frames) and 'backbone_domain_rmsd' fails the one-entry-per-frame value set, as the executed report shows.

rationale:
## Repair summary

All review findings are corrected without changing any scientific requirement, tolerance, covered artifact, check identity or the grader program itself (null; its executed behavior was correct in every recorded control).

1. **Cross-file Time contract mismatch resolved in prose, code unchanged.** The 'time_column_consistency' check description previously promised a 1e-9 tolerance, but the grader enforces exact parsed-float identity across the four tables (a set of per-file values is collected and any distinct value fails; the 1e-9 tolerance is applied only in each file's per-row comparison against the reference). Exact identity is the correct and stricter scientific requirement — the tables sample one trajectory — so the description was corrected to state exact equality of parsed values, with the 1e-9 rule explicitly confined to the per-file reference comparison. The addendum already states 'identical Time (ns) value' and is retained unchanged, so contract and implementation now agree.

2. **Quoted-numbers contract mismatch resolved in prose, code unchanged.** The addendum now states that CSV field quoting is a serialization detail accepted exactly when the unquoted content satisfies the same parsed-content rules; the open_closed_rmsd_structure check description dropped its contradictory 'unquoted' clause. No comparison value, tolerance or equivalence is altered, so no acceptance criterion is weakened.

3. **Probe annotations corrected.** The two copy-paste check_ids errors ('core-ca-ragged-row' → core_ca_rmsd; 'nonfinite-value-resid' → resid_weighted_rmsd) are fixed as originally directed. Additionally, per the review's consistency convention ('the checks that actually reject the mutated files'): every wrong_solution value/row/column mutation probe now lists 'trajectory_tables_structure' where the grader's aggregate structural check in fact fails alongside the file-specific scientific check (verified against each probe's executed report); 'time-single-file-drift' additionally lists 'core_ca_rmsd' (per-row 1e-9 Time comparison in the affected file) and 'time_column_consistency' (broken cross-file exact identity); 'truncated-frames-lazy' additionally lists 'mass_weighted_rmsd' (missing frames, nonfinite value) and 'time_column_consistency' (row-count mismatch). The falsified rationale on 'backbone-domain-values-bias' is rewritten to accurately state that the aggregate structure check also fails (it aggregates all per-file value-mismatch problems) while the file's structural dimensions remain well-formed; the same truthful wording was applied to the other aggregate-failure rationales. All classifications, scripts, names and focus values are unchanged; scientific wrong-result coverage is retained on every check.

## Evidence and limitations

The csv.reader unquoting behavior and the exact cross-file Time comparison are facts of the unchanged grader source, confirmed by the review's inspection; no new measurement or code change was required. The grader, reference outputs, five endpoints, tolerance model (|s−r| ≤ max(3e-6 Å, 1e-9·|r|), reference denominator; 1e-9 absolute per-file Time rule) and row-alignment/coverage rules are identical to the candidate whose scientific scope the review approved. Residual known limitations are unchanged from the suite record: the Time column is a reader convention on a timestamp-free DCD (graded at disclosed 1e-9 absolute per-file, exact cross-file), and frame-0 self-comparison values (~1e-7 Å) are representation-level indistinguishable below the 3e-6 Å floor, far below any observed wrong-method shift. The controller should re-run all frozen controls, especially the re-annotated probes, against the revised candidate hash.
